title: Treasury coupon announcement (10-Year TIPS NEW ISSUE + 20-Year bond reopening + 6/13/26/52-week bills) — where the 2027 TIPS size actually prints
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-10y-tips-2027-01-21 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised. Six securities carry `Thursday, January 14, 2027` as their announcement date, read verbatim from that text: `6-Week  BILL`, `13-Week  BILL`, `26-Week  BILL` and `52-Week  BILL` (all auctioned Tuesday, January 19, 2027), `20-Year  BONDR` (auctioned Wednesday, January 20, 2027, settled Friday, January 22, 2027) and `10-Year  TIPST` (auctioned Thursday, January 21, 2027, settled Friday, January 29, 2027). The PDF's own legend, also read verbatim, is `T --denotes TIPS` and `R --denotes reopening`. The 11:00 a.m. ET announcement time is Treasury convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-10y-tips-2027-01-21 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09). PROPOSED BECAUSE IT IS THE VENUE, NOT THE ECHO. The proposer's whole information content is a single number — the 10-Year TIPS new-issue size — and this is the session it becomes public, seven days before the auction. The calendar already tracks the analogous announcement for every 2026 coupon block (treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-09-10 through -2026-11-19), so the class is established; this is its first 2027 instance and the first one that sizes a TIPS NEW ISSUE rather than a reopening. WHY THAT DISTINCTION IS THE POINT: the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12 ledger's central finding is that a TIPS size change has never expressed at a reopening — every step in the 10-Year series (13 -> 14 -> 15 -> 16 -> 17 -> 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21) landed on a January or July new issue. 2027-01-14 is therefore the first date on which that claim can be scored rather than restated. SIZE EXPECTATION, for whoever researches it, with both sides stated: the base case is $21B (flat), because 2026 is the first year since 2020 in which no TIPS tenor's new issue rose at all — 0 of 4 transitions, against 4 of 5 in 2025 — and because the 30-Year has held $9B for six consecutive new issues, so a long freeze is ordinary in this complex. The live counter-case is that the 10-Year series has never held one size for four consecutive new issues: its runs are 13Bx3, 14Bx3, 15Bx1, 16Bx2, 17Bx3, 18Bx1, 19Bx1, 20Bx1 and now 21Bx3, and each of the three prior runs that reached three was ended by a step-up at the fourth, 3 of 3 (fiscaldata auctions_query, `inflation_index_security: Yes`, back to 2018-01-01, 105 rows, pulled 2026-09-09). ALSO ON THIS SHEET: the 20-Year bond is a reopening (`R`), whose base rate is 13 consecutive new issues at $16B and 29 reopenings at $13B per the 11-12 sibling. Proposed as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
